test_cases.title: Successful login with valid credentials
test_cases.precondition: A user account exists with email tester@vantagefitness.com
test_cases.expected: User is redirected to the dashboard and a welcome banner appears
test_cases.actual: User was redirected to the dashboard and welcome banner appeared

test_cases.title: Login fails with an invalid password
test_cases.precondition: A user account exists with email tester@vantagefitness.com
test_cases.expected: An inline error message 'Invalid email or password' is displayed and the user stays on the login page
test_cases.actual: The server returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error instead of a validation message
test_cases.notes: Reproducible 100% of the time on Chrome 124 and Firefox 125

test_cases.title: Remember me persists the session across a browser restart
test_cases.precondition: A user account exists. Browser cookies are enabled.
steps: Reopen the browser and navigate back to the app
test_cases.expected: The user is still logged in without being prompted to re-authenticate
test_cases.actual: Not tested this run — deferred to next sprint due to pending cookie-policy changes
test_cases.notes: Blocked by Sprint 14 cookie-policy ticket #1892. Will re-test in Sprint 15.

bugs.title: Login endpoint returns HTTP 500 on invalid password instead of 401
bugs.description: When a user submits an incorrect password, the authentication service throws an unhandled exception that propagates as a 500 Internal Server Error. The full Java stack trace is exposed in the response body, which is both a UX failure and a potential security risk.
steps: Enter a valid email and an intentionally wrong password
Inspect the HTTP response in the browser developer tools
bugs.expected: HTTP 401 Unauthorised with a JSON body: { "error": "Invalid email or password" }
bugs.actual: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error — full Java stack trace visible in the response body
bugs.notes: Stack trace exposes internal class names and file paths. Treat as a security issue.

bugs.title: Welcome banner displays user database ID instead of display name
bugs.description: After a successful login, the dashboard header shows the numeric database primary key (e.g. 'Welcome, 10042') instead of the user's human-readable display name (e.g. 'Welcome, Meghna Dutta'). This was introduced in release v2.4.1.
steps: Log in with any valid credentials
Observe the welcome banner in the top-right area of the dashboard
bugs.expected: Banner reads 'Welcome, [display name]' — e.g. 'Welcome, Meghna Dutta'
bugs.actual: Banner reads 'Welcome, 10042' (the user's numeric database ID)
bugs.notes: Fix is in code review on PR #88. Regression introduced in v2.4.1 when the user-profile service was refactored.
